messages:
incident-bot: Pager: HIGH - us-west2 GPU pool saturation > 95% (auto-escalation). Fallbacks triggered. Link: https://incidents.internal/redwood/1999991111 :fire:
devin (oncall): seeing high queue depths for inference-rt-us-west2, requests backing up into retry layer. Dropping tail latency to 1.8s -> 4s. Noticed many low-priority batch jobs started at 08:12 UTC.
mara: confirmed - autoscaler created extra thin-prov nodes but they were preempted, then scheduler moved pods and we got cold starts. Some Dedicated tenants moved to fallback-model-small.
ajay: looks like quantized model variant (q4_0) fallback produced hallucinations for a few customers? CS flagged 3 customer complaints.
beatrice: customers impacted reported higher error rates and truncated responses. CS ticket numbers: CS-8891, CS-8892, CS-8895.
devin (oncall): mitigation steps I took so far:
```
1) Issued pause on low-priority offline workloads: /runbook pause_low_priority_batches
2) Manual scale: kubectl scale deployment autoscaler -n infra --replicas=0 -> then re-enabled with min=4
3) Forced eviction of spot thin-prov nodes in us-west2 to let stable nodes reclaim slots
```
mara: thanks. I also bumped up dedicated-gpu-pool-usw2 from 8 -> 12 (hotfix) to buy time. Monitoring after bump shows queue falling.
sre-lead: was there a config that allowed the autoscaler to oversubscribe spot nodes and then not fallback gracefully? We need root cause later but quick question: any regions already failing over?
kevin: eu-west1 handled some traffic automatically (smart-routing), about ~9% of requests routed. Latency in eu was fine. No customer-visible degradation for EU tenants.
cs-sam: chasing affected customers now. Notified an enterprise customer about degraded quality, offered rollback to previous model. They accepted temporary rollback for non-critical traffic.
ajay: the problematic behavior: fallback to q4_0 variant + shortened sequence lengths combined with request batching mismatch -> truncated outputs. We'll capture a reproduction set.
beatrice: logging: request IDs and sample prompts captured. Dropping into /sre/logs/1999991111/ for review.
devin (oncall): scheduling post-incident review. Proposed bridge: tomorrow 09:00 UTC, 60m. Attendees: oncall, SRE, runtime team, product + CS.
sre-lead: action items we should track now (short-term):
- AI: validate autoscaler thresholds and spot eviction handling (owner: ajay, due: 1999991511)
- AR: add guardrail to prevent fallback to smaller quantized variant for enterprise tenants (owner: mara, due: 1999991611)
- Log: aggregate impacted request ids and surface to CS (owner: cs-sam, due: 1999991411)
- Runbook: update evacuation playbook with explicit step to pause low-priority batches (owner: beatrice, due: 1999991611)
- Observability: add dashboard for fallback-model-rate by customer tier (owner: liz, due: 1999991511)

liz: I'll add the dashboard tiles and set a 5m alert if fallback-model usage for any dedicated customer > 0.5%.
kevin: suggest a medium-term mitigation: pre-warm a tiny warm pool of 4 stable nodes in each region to reduce cold-starts. Draft config:
```yaml
prewarm-pools:
  us-west2: 4
  eu-west1: 2
  asia-east1: 2
```
We should evaluate cost vs. outage risk.
mara: agree on prewarm. Also need model router to prefer non-quantized variants for VIP customers even if capacity tight.
beatrice: postmortem meeting scheduled: link to calendar invite https://calendar.internal/event/1999991200 — please RSVP.
devin (oncall): temporary status: incident resolved for now, queue back to normal, fallback rates down to baseline. Leaving this thread open for follow-ups.
cs-sam: updated customers with status and ETA for permanent fix. They want a follow-up report after postmortem.
ajay: capturing repro steps and sampling failure traces, will push to GH issues: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/issues/5102
sre-lead: longest outstanding blocker: lack of a fast soft-eviction policy that preserves affinity for dedicated tenants. Add to roadmap.
kevin: noted. I'll draft a cost analysis for prewarm change.
beatrice: will drive runbook PR and include exact kubectl snippets we used, so future oncall can run them fast.
mara: owner matrix sanity-check: ajay (autoscaler fix), mara (router/model-guard), beatrice (runbook), liz (dashboard), kevin (prewarm cost), cs-sam (customer comms).
devin (oncall): assigning temporary incident label: capacity-evacuation-1999991111 and creating follow-up tracker.
incident-bot: Incident closed (auto): all severity metrics returned to baseline. Postmortem: scheduled.
devin (oncall): closing comments: good coordination, quick manual scaling was key. Please add any other follow-ups below and owners.
kevin: +1 to adding a short checklist in the runbook: "If autoscaler jumps to spot-heavy, pause low-priority batches, scale dedicated pool, route critical tenants to fallback region"
mara: adding to runbook now.
beatrice: PR submitted for runbook updates: https://git.internal/redwood/docs/pulls/872
cs-sam: will compile customer impact summary for postmortem doc.
ajay: uploading trace dump to the incident folder.
(reacts): devin (oncall) :thumbsup:  mara :eyes: beatrice :sparkles:
